name: CPP-ML-Interface
tagline: Modular C++ coupling middleware for low-latency CFD and Machine Learning inference
description:
A modular, generic C++ middleware designed to couple complex Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) solvers with machine learning models. Developed as a core part of a Master's Thesis at RWTH Aachen University (Chair for High Performance Computing, i12), it redesigns and generalizes the legacy solver-specific CPP-ML-Interface-MAIA, abstracting underlying communication libraries into a unified, configuration-driven coupling boundary.

The middleware is optimized for and benchmarked on the Claix23 cluster. Hardware targets include dual-socket CPU nodes equipped with 2x Intel Xeon 8468 (Sapphire Rapids) processors, and GPU nodes equipped with 4x NVIDIA H100 acceleration cards, which are critical for low-level CPU parallel execution configurations (such as intra/inter-op threads, OpenMP tasking, and Slurm core affinity bindings).

The project is developed inside a larger workspace structure (smartsim_playground) which coordinates several benchmark and validation utilities:

```
smartsim/ (smartsim_playground workspace)
├── CPP-ML-Interface (Redesigned generic interface)
│   ├── extern/AIxeleratorService
│   ├── extern/SmartRedis
│   └── extern/phydll
├── cpu_benchmark (CPU/GPU inference threading & core affinity benchmarks)
├── lmod_dependencies (Z3-based HPC module resolver)
├── mini_app (Toy CFD solver used for prototyping)
└── module_test (Integration testing with ~600 combinations)
```

The interface will soon replace the predecessor library in the MMCP project to couple the MMCP_transformer with the m-aia solver.
purpose: To eliminate low-performance file-based and socket bottlenecks in High-Performance Computing (HPC) by providing a low-latency, platform-independent in-memory data path between physical simulations and AI models.
strengths: Redesigned from solver-specific code into a highly generic, modular header-only interface
Integrates heterogeneous coupling libraries (SmartSim, PhyDLL, AIxeleratorService) under a configuration-based layer
Supports reflection-free subclass registration via an automatic python-clang parsing registry script
Critically evaluates low-level CPU parallel execution (intra/inter-op threads, OpenMP, core affinity)
limitations: Currently restricted to PyTorch (TorchScript) backend implementations
Performance is bound by underlying library interconnects (e.g. Redis database roundtrips in SmartSim)
Requires matching compiler/Clang versions for the registry generator script
installation:
# Setup the cluster environment (modules for compiler, python, clang, etc.).
# A cluster-specific 'install.sh' is provided for Claix23/RWTH, but manual
# configuration is needed on other systems.
# 
# Note: Building and compiling the external submodules/dependencies
# (SmartSim, PhyDLL, AIxeleratorService) is required and exceeds the scope
# of this quick start page.

# Clone the repository and submodules:
git clone --recursive git@github.com:chrisb09/CPP-ML-Interface.git
cd CPP-ML-Interface

# Install python dependencies for registry generation:
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run your system/cluster build wrapper script:
./build.sh
usage:
# Run verification executable with sample config and dummy steps:
./build/cpp_ml_interface_executable --config-file example.config.toml --behavior 100
roadmap: Integrate the generic prototype into the MMCP simulation project to couple MMCP_transformer and m-aia
Evaluate zero-copy shared-memory coupling implementations to bypass TCP overhead
Add support for ONNX Runtime and TensorFlow C++ backends
